disposition_meaning.develop: apparently clean and novel enough for a deeper proposal brief, not yet approved for filing
disposition_meaning.compose: prefer explicit composition or a small example using existing constructs
disposition_meaning.covered: a current register proposal already targets the same ambiguity
disposition_meaning.ordinary: ordinary explicit wording is shorter or safer than a new marker
disposition_meaning.research_only: interesting linguistic case without a convincing general Ainglish repair

cards.ambiguity: Does a result hold separately in every group, or only for all groups pooled into one aggregate?
cards.consequence: A receiver may apply a universal per-group claim when only an aggregate statistic supports it, a direct ecological-inference error.
cards.candidate_mapping: The first says the clause is true separately for every member group in G. The second says it is true only after the members of G are pooled; it makes no per-group claim.
cards.collision_note: Related group and set constructs concern actors, population completeness, or cross-group distinctness; none found declares the statistical aggregation level.

cards.ambiguity: Does 'consult any qualifying organisation' require one qualifying organisation or every one?
cards.consequence: A workflow can satisfy one existential consultation when universal consultation was required, or contact everyone unnecessarily.
cards.candidate_mapping: The first requires one member of a named non-empty set; the second requires the action separately for every member.
cards.collision_note: Existing cardinality and distributivity constructs can express the two readings; a new surface risks duplicating both.

cards.ambiguity: After two topics, does 'this' refer to one topic or both?
cards.consequence: A receiver can request or update the wrong record.
cards.candidate_mapping: Name the intended referent or referent set explicitly instead of relying on an unbound demonstrative.
cards.collision_note: Explicit references are already common in Ainglish forms; naming the object in ordinary English is generally clearer than adding a two-pole marker.

cards.ambiguity: Does 'will' make a promise, report a plan, or forecast an event?
cards.consequence: A receiver can treat a prediction as a commitment or execute a plan that was only forecast.
cards.collision_note: The register already has the exact promise/plan/forecast split.

cards.ambiguity: Does 'may' grant permission or say that an event is possible?
cards.consequence: A receiver can mistake a forecast for authority or miss a granted option.
cards.collision_note: The register already has the exact permission/possibility split.

cards.ambiguity: Does 'tested' say that a procedure ran, or that the subject passed it?
cards.consequence: A receiver can infer successful validation from mere test execution.
cards.collision_note: The register already has the exact run/passed split, motivated by this failure class.

cards.ambiguity: Does 'assure X' require checking X, making X true, or merely taking reasonable steps?
cards.consequence: A procedure can finish without either a measurable check or the promised state.
cards.candidate_mapping: Name the observable check and criterion, or issue a guarantee-strength instruction, rather than preserving the vague verb.
cards.collision_note: Existing attempt/ensure and checked-at constructs cover the force and evidence axes; the source argues for measurable actions, not a new synonym.

cards.ambiguity: Has an event merely been observed, or has an authority formally assigned it an operative status?
cards.consequence: Goals, reporting duties, authority, and priorities may remain unset even when everyone knows the physical event occurred.
cards.candidate_mapping: The first records an event claim. The second records a formal status act by a named authority; neither silently entails the other.
cards.collision_note: Observation provenance plus an authority-labelled operative decision appears to express the distinction without a new monolithic pair.

cards.ambiguity: Does silence permit action, require holding, or simply leave the state unknown?
cards.consequence: A safety-critical action may begin without positive coordination.
cards.collision_note: The register already has the explicit go-on-silence versus hold-for-yes distinction.

cards.ambiguity: Is a bare number a heading, speed, altitude, count, time, or another typed quantity?
cards.consequence: A correct magnitude can be applied to the wrong operational field.
cards.candidate_mapping: Attach an ordinary unit or field name to every load-bearing number.
cards.collision_note: Ordinary units and field labels are already compact, widely standardised, and more interoperable than a new Ainglish marker.

cards.ambiguity: Is 'cooking' the action being performed on apples, or a modifier naming a kind of apple?
cards.consequence: A parser can recover a process when the text names an object class, or vice versa.
cards.candidate_mapping: Expose the parse explicitly when lexical category is load-bearing.
cards.collision_note: The ambiguity is real, but the proposed repair is heavier than ordinary rephrasing and lacks a reusable flagship surface.

cards.ambiguity: What scope and acceptance criterion does 'complete' assert?
cards.consequence: A receiver can stop after activity ends while required outcomes remain unverified.
cards.collision_note: The ratified stopped/done-under/complete-for family already separates cessation, criteria, and requirement scope.

cards.consequence: Different agents can satisfy the same instruction at incompatible cadences.
cards.candidate_mapping: Use an ordinary explicit recurrence rule.
cards.collision_note: The biweekly split covers one famous case; generic cadence is better represented with established schedule expressions than a new semantic pair.

cards.ambiguity: Does a provision describe, create, enable, or authorise an action?
cards.consequence: A receiver can mistake capability for permission or descriptive text for an operative rule.
cards.candidate_mapping: Use the ordinary verb that names the intended legal or operational force.
cards.collision_note: Existing permission/capability markers plus ordinary 'specifies' cover the useful axes more cleanly than a four-way lexical replacement.

cards.ambiguity: Does 'provide entertainment' mean offer hospitality or supply entertainment as a trade product?
cards.consequence: The same phrase can select different legal and accounting treatment.
cards.candidate_mapping: Name the concrete transaction rather than preserving the polysemous phrase.
cards.collision_note: The ambiguity is domain-specific and ordinary concrete wording is clearer than a register-wide marker.
